videos.t: SEQUENCING A ROBOT DRUM KIT USING THE ELEKTRON OCTATRACK MKII
videos.desc:
This is a live track recorded in a single take using an acoustic robot drum kit and the #Elektron Octatrack MkII. There are no pre-recorded samples or synths and all the melodic sounds are made using comb filters and flangers modulated by LFOs and resampled in various ways on the fly.  The drums are MIDI sequenced using the Octatrack, which also does all the live sound processing.
Got to love the #Octatrack

You can download the track here:
https://lomondcampbell.bandcamp.com/track/unravelled

This MIDI to parallel board from J Omega does all the conversion on the #robotdrums:
http://www.j-ome

videos.t: HOW TO SEQUENCE YOUR EURORACK SYSTEM WITH A RECORD PLAYER
videos.desc:
Convert any turntable in to a programmable rotary gate sequencer for modular #Eurorack systems with just a few components and a simple bit of coding. 

Components:
x1 #Arduino Nano
x4 proximity switches / reed switches
x4 10K resistors
x4 3.5mm mono jacks
x4 LEDs (optional)
x4 100 Ohm resistors (optional)
x4 SPDT toggle switches (optional)
x1 vero board
.... + some camdenboss terminal blocks if you're in to that kind of thing. 

Here's the link to the code, schematics and diagram:

videos.t: SYNTHESIZER TRAVELER F1 - THE VINTAGE KORG WAH WAH PEDAL THAT THINKS IT'S A SYNTH
videos.desc:
This is the Synthesizer Traveler F-1 pedal. 

It was built in 1972 by Keio Electronic Laboratories (which would become known as KORG) and there weren't many built.  It’s essentially a bombproof WAH WAH pedal with some added extras.  This is a short demo video exploring some of the unusual features and terminology.  As it behaves like a primitive monosynth I decided to hook it up to the modular system and mess around.

I built an 18th century harmonograph and connected it to a 21st century modular synthesiser.
A harmonograph is an old scientific device that uses pendulums to create illustrations of harmonic motion, called lissajous figures.  On this harmonograph each pendulum is connected to a sensor which triggers different elements of the synthesiser so that every time it makes a drawing, it also plays an accompanying synth soundtrack.  There's also a contact mic on the drawing board to pick up the sound of the pen. 

It uses three pendulums - two connected in a linear way to the pen and one rotary pendulu

videos.t: The making of LŪP - the instrument that wants to be Basinski and Reich
videos.desc: This is a video about the concepts behind LŪP and how I went about making it.  I was commissioned to build a custom tape-looper instrument and wanted the machine to embody the compositional ideas of the two esteemed New York avant-garde composers - William Basinski and Steve Reich.  It plays 10 second tape loops which ‘disintegrate’ over time as the tape passes near to a rotating magnetic disc.  This rotating disc also provides a clock and drives two eccentric cams which sends out ever-shifting phase patterns. videos.t: LŪP  -  custom tape looper and phase pattern generator
videos.desc: LŪP came about when I was commissioned to build a custom tape-looper instrument.  I wanted the machine to embody the compositional ideas of the two esteemed New York avant-garde composers, William Basinski and Steve Reich.  It plays 10 second tape loops which ‘disintegrate’ over time as the tape passes near to a rotating magnetic disc.  This rotating disc also provides a clock and drives two eccentric cams which sends out ever-shifting phase patterns.   You can hook the machine up to a modular synthesiser and process the disintegrating tape loops while generating Reichian phase shifting patter

This version of the Harmonograph Synth was created for an exhibition in Edinburgh.  I didn't want to exhibit my modular synth so I used Pure Data to create a generative music patch.  As with before, the pendulums trigger musical events but they also trigger sporadic poems by four UK poets.  This one, called Fill Your Basket is by Hollie McNish.

​Julija Pustovrh was the first participant.  She is a Slovenian born artist now living and working in Edinburgh, Scotland, UK. Her background is in Landscape Architecture but more recently she has been focusing on ceramics. Julija has always drawn inspiration from nature and is currently working on an ongoing project exploring the connection between Scottish landscapes and coastal features.

videos.t: LOST LOOPS LIVE on a DIY MIDI CONTROLLER #1
videos.desc:
This performance makes use of sounds from my album Lost Loops using a DIY MIDI interface to sample and manipulate the sounds.  I used some nice old rotary switches, part of a mechanical keyboard, LED toggles and various other tactile controls, all housed in a bruised attaché case.  At the heart of the interface is a Doepfer Pocket Electronic putting out MIDI CC data, converted to CV by the Polyend Poly 2 for MIDI to CV then mapped out to various parameters on a modular synth. 

Found out more about lost Loops here:
 https://lomondcampbell.lnk.to/lostloops

Looking for a meaningful way to incorporate language into music that bypassed the convention of hearing words being said or sung, I built The Unsung Machine.  The Unsung Machine is an experimental interface that introduces aleatoric events into music through the act of entering words on the device.

The Muonophone is a machine I built that allows me to make music using muon detectors.  These muon detectors pick up harmless radiation caused by cosmic rays interacting with the Earth’s atmosphere. The Muonophone will be exhibited at The French Institute in Edinburgh from 8th - 25th August for the Edinburgh Fringe as part of a show called MŮO.  The installation is open 11am - 5pm and is free entry.  I'll also be playing 9 live shows with the Muonophone during the festival.
